principles: Restore only the bucket paths proven by the approved stash split plan
Prefer focused smoke evidence over narrative confidence
Keep dev-memory non-authoritative and separate from Lattice gate evidence
Fail closed if the hunk cannot be verified without restoring runtime data
drivers: Bucket A is isolated to dev-memory read compatibility
The user asked to execute the approved plan without arbitrary optimization
The stashed runtime data file must remain local and uncommitted
Other buckets have different risks and must stay separate

options.name: A: Execute Bucket A only with focused smoke test
pros: Allows a narrow proof of legacy read fallback
Keeps data file and other buckets untouched
cons: Leaves Bucket B-D for later stories and Bucket E deferred until repro

options.name: B: Apply all dev-memory-related stash content including data and gitignore
pros: Would move all visually related dev-memory stash paths together
cons: Would violate the explicit no data-file restore rule
Would mix runtime data policy with code behavior
Would risk committing local non-source memory data

options.name: C: Skip Bucket A and move to documentation Bucket D
pros: Could deliver a visible document artifact sooner
cons: Would ignore the approved safe first bucket after B-70f5
Would leave the dev-memory compatibility hunk unclassified

chosen: A: Execute Bucket A only with focused smoke test
rationale: Choose Bucket A only because the stash split plan requires one future Lattice story per bucket, and this hunk can be mechanically verified without applying the whole stash or restoring runtime data.

preMortem.scenario: The story accidentally restores the stashed dev-memory data file
preMortem.trigger: A broad git restore command or untracked restore is used
preMortem.consequence: Local runtime data becomes tracked or staged as source
preMortem.mitigation: Use explicit tracked-path restore only and verify git status excludes .lattice/dev-memory/experience.jsonl

preMortem.scenario: Legacy .koala fallback becomes a write target
preMortem.trigger: Path helpers are reused for append/write behavior
preMortem.consequence: Lattice writes new assets under legacy .koala, violating migration rules
preMortem.mitigation: Smoke test write behavior and keep append paths resolved to .lattice only

preMortem.scenario: Dev-memory entries are treated as gate or Authority evidence
preMortem.trigger: Tests only check presence of entries and ignore authority fields
preMortem.consequence: Non-authoritative advisory memory could be overclaimed
preMortem.mitigation: Smoke test gateEvidence=false and authority=non_authoritative and record Authority productionDone=false
